result:
All 36 tests pass (this is currently the only `*AgentTest.java` file in the tree).

I created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDateParserAgentTest.java`, in the same package so it can use `FastDateParser`'s protected constructor and package-private helpers directly without depending on any other test class. It covers: happy-path parsing, partial consumption and offset start positions, error paths (invalid input, literal mismatches, out-of-range start index, integer overflow) returning `null`/throwing `ParseException` instead of leaking internal exceptions, the greedy-field `maxWidth` boundary, equality/hashCode/toString contracts, null-argument handling in the constructor, malformed-pattern errors (unterminated quote, unsupported letter, invalid ISO-8601 width), two-digit year century rollover, ISO-8601/GMT timezone strategies, locale month-name parsing (including case-insensitivity and failure), hour boundary strategies (`hh`=12→0, `kk`=24→0), week-year (`Y`) resolution, serialization round-trip, the static cache-clear helper, and a couple of package-private utilities (`TimeZoneStrategy.skipTimeZone`, `JAPANESE_IMPERIAL`).

One planned case (the `isWeekDateSupported()==false` fallback) wasn't testable since that method is `final` in `GregorianCalendar` and `Calendar` is otherwise too heavy to subclass minimally, so I dropped it rather than force something unreliable.
